NovaBio Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad and wait for further instructions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Lisa Chen, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBio Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are David Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Thompson, CEO of NovaBio Therapeutics.

David Thompson, CEO:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning, everyone. NovaBio Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust demand for our flagship oncology asset OncoVita, the successful ramp of our new migraine prophylaxis drug NeuroVex, and continued execution across our rare disease and immunology franchises. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including expanding market share in high-growth therapeutic areas and advancing a deep pipeline of next-generation therapies.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, with a focus on our marketing and sales effectiveness metrics that are powering portfolio growth, the strong product revenue contributions from our key drug franchises including volume and pricing dynamics, our R&D expense allocation and pipeline investment priorities, and a detailed operating expense analysis. 

We are particularly excited about NeuroVex and its potential to achieve rapid market penetration similar to recent neurology launches, targeting peak sales exceeding $2 billion by 2028.

Now, I will turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins, CFO:
Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $1,450 million, an increase of 19% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by volume growth in OncoVita from label expansions and new patient starts, alongside NeuroVex's strong launch momentum and share gains in immunology and rare diseases.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $265 million, or $1.25 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $340 million, or $1.60 per share.

Our operating expenses were $680 million, reflecting continued investment in R&D to fuel our pipeline while optimizing SG&A through data-driven efficiencies. We continue to invest heavily in innovation to support long-term growth. Our cash position remains strong at $2.6 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenue of $5.9 billion to $6.1 billion, non-GAAP EPS of $6.50 to $6.80, and R&D spend of $1.48 billion to $1.52 billion.

Thank you, David, and good afternoon, everyone. Moving now to our marketing and sales effectiveness metrics, which continue to underpin our double-digit revenue growth across the portfolio. As you know, in the highly competitive pharma and biotech landscape—where we're going head-to-head with the likes of Merck's Keytruda in immuno-oncology and Novartis' Entresto in CV—we've doubled down on data-driven strategies to maximize every dollar of our $1.2 billion SG&A spend this year. I'll walk you through the key KPIs, trends, regional nuances, and the technical initiatives fueling our outperformance, all tied to our core franchises: OncoVita, our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific generating $2.8 billion in 2023 trailing twelve-month sales; RareGuard, our gene therapy for Pompe disease; and the recently launched NeuroVex for migraine prophylaxis.

First, let's start with sales force productivity, a cornerstone metric in our field rep model. Our 1,800-strong specialty sales force—optimized via AI-driven territory management in Veeva CRM—achieved an average of 28 high-quality HCP interactions per rep per week in Q3, up 12% year-over-year and ahead of our internal target of 25. This translated to a 22% lift in new prescription (NRx) conversion rates, from 14% to 17.1%, particularly in oncology where OncoVita's NRx share in metastatic NSCLC climbed to 18.2% from 15.4% a year ago, per IQVIA data. Total prescriptions (TRx) for OncoVita grew 16% QoQ, outpacing the category's 9% expansion amid headwinds from biosimilar erosion on Roche's Avastin.

On the digital and omnichannel front, we've seen explosive adoption post our 2022 digital transformation. HCP engagement via our proprietary provider portal—powered by Salesforce Health Cloud and integrated with real-world evidence from TriNetX—hit 4.2 million unique logins YTD, a 35% YoY surge, with 62% of interactions now digital versus 41% in 2022. This shift has boosted our share of voice (SOV) to 27% in immuno-oncology digital channels, per Komodo Health analytics, ahead of BMS's Opdivo at 22%. Patient-facing DTC efforts in the US for NeuroVex generated a 28% increase in branded search volume on Google Trends, correlating to a 19% NRx uplift in the first 90 days post-launch—mirroring the successful ramps of Eli Lilly's Emgality.

ROI metrics tell an even stronger story. Our blended marketing ROI reached 4.8x in Q3—meaning $4.80 in incremental revenue per dollar invested—up from 3.9x last year, driven by precision targeting. For instance, our programmatic ad spend on platforms like DV360 yielded a 5.2x return in the US commercial segment, while KOL (key opinion leader) engagement programs—featuring virtual advisory boards with 150+ top-tier oncologists—delivered a 6.1x ROI via 14% higher adherence rates on OncoVita. Cost per TRx acquired fell 11% to $145, thanks to machine learning models predicting HCP prescribing behavior with 87% accuracy.

Regionally, performance varies but remains robust. In the US, which accounts for 62% of our sales, payer pull-through was stellar: 92% formulary coverage for OncoVita under Medicare Part D, with rebates averaging 28% versus the industry's 32% per SSR Health. This drove a 21% YoY TRx growth, bolstered by our "VitaPath" patient support hub, which enrolled 45,000 patients and reduced discontinuation by 15% through AI-chatbot adherence nudges. In Europe, facing EMA pricing scrutiny and HTA delays akin to those plaguing AstraZeneca's Tagrisso, we grew 11% in ex-US developed markets—led by Germany and France—via value-based pricing pilots that secured 85% reimbursement at launch list price for RareGuard. Emerging markets, 12% of sales, exploded 32% YoY, with China TRx for OncoVita up 41% on NMPA approval and partnerships with local distributors like Sinopharm, though we note tariff risks under evolving US-China trade dynamics.

Key technical initiatives accelerating this: Our "PrecisionLaunch" AI platform, built on Google Cloud Vertex AI, segments HCPs into 12 micro-cohorts based on prescribing patterns, treatment gaps, and social determinants—yielding a 24% efficiency gain in sales routing. We've also rolled out closed-loop marketing automation with Marketo Engage, closing the feedback loop from ad impression to Rx fill in under 7 days for 68% of campaigns. Looking ahead, we'll pilot blockchain-tracked patient journeys with IBM for RareGuard to combat counterfeiting in APAC.

Strategically, these metrics aren't just vanity—they're fueling sustainable growth. Our 15% share gain in addressable immuno-oncology TAM positions OncoVita for $4 billion peak sales by 2027, while NeuroVex's launch efficiency—hitting 10% market share in 6 months—validates our "Launch360" playbook, which has de-risked four launches since 2021. Amid biosimilar threats and IRP (inflation reduction act) clawbacks, we're allocating 20% more to digital (now 45% of budget) to future-proof against sales force shrinkage industry-wide.

Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. I'll now walk you through our product revenue performance by key franchise, with a deep dive into volume and price dynamics. As you know, NovaBio's portfolio is anchored in three high-growth areas: Oncology, Immunology, and Rare Diseases, representing 100% of our $1.28 billion in Q3 product net sales – up 18% year-over-year, or 16% on a CER basis. This marks our 11th straight quarter of double-digit growth, driven by a balanced mix of volume expansion from label extensions and market share gains, partially offset by targeted pricing strategies amid payer pressures.

Let me break it down franchise by franchise, starting with our largest contributor, Oncology, which delivered $785 million in Q3 net sales – 61% of total product revenue and up 22% YoY. OncoVita, our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific antibody and blockbuster franchise akin to the Keytruda-Opdivo duopoly, accounted for 95% of this at $746 million, up 24% YoY. Volume grew 19% YoY, fueled by 12% higher TRx – totaling 285,000 scripts – and a 7% increase in patient persistence rates to 78% at 12 months, thanks to our OncoVita PRO patient support program, which boosted adherence via AI-driven refill reminders and copay assistance. We saw 14,500 new patient starts, up 16% YoY, driven by the recent EMA and FDA label expansions into frontline MSI-high endometrial cancer and adjuvant NSCLC, capturing 22% share in those indications per IQVIA data.

Geographically, U.S. volumes surged 25% YoY on 28% NRx growth, while ex-U.S. – EU5 and Japan – rose 12%, tempered by slower reimbursement in Germany post-AMNOG reassessment. Pricing contributed 3% to growth: ASP held steady at $162,000 per patient-year in the U.S. after 4.5% WAC increase, but net ASP dipped 1% to $118,000 due to higher 360-value-based agreements – now covering 45% of lives – and biosimilar rebate creep from Roche's Tecentriq lookalikes entering select markets. Ex-U.S. net ASP grew 2% on favorable tender wins in China. Looking ahead, we're scaling our Singapore facility by 30% capacity with continuous manufacturing tech to support OncoVita's next-gen subcutaneous formulation, filing for approval H1 2025, which could add 10-15% volume uplift via office-based administration.

Moving to Immunology, $320 million in Q3 net sales – 25% of total, up 14% YoY. ImmunoShield, our IL-23/IL-17 dual inhibitor mirroring Tremfya's profile in psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis, drove $298 million, or 16% YoY growth. Volume was the star here, up 12% YoY with 112,000 TRx and 9,800 NRx – gaining 3 points of share to 18% in moderate-to-severe psoriasis per Symphony Health. This reflects our "ShieldFirst" direct-to-patient hub, which enrolled 65% of new starters and improved 6-month adherence to 82% via subcutaneous auto-injector tech upgrades. U.S. volumes jumped 18% on combo therapy momentum with JAK inhibitors post our Phase 3 SYNERGY trial readout, while EU volumes grew 8% despite biosimilar erosion from Samsung Bioepis' versions of Stelara, now at 15% market penetration.

Price contributed 2% to growth: U.S. net ASP stable at $52,000 per patient-year after 5% WAC hike, offset by PBM rebates rising to 48% under CVS Caremark's formulary shift. Ex-U.S., ASP grew 4% on ASP pricing reforms in France. Strategically, we're mitigating patent expiry in 2027 with ImmunoShield NXT, our oral small-molecule follow-on entering Phase 3, and a $250 million bolt-on acquisition of a UK-based IL-36 asset to fortify our pipeline against AbbVie's Skyrizi dominance.

Finally, Rare Diseases – $175 million, 14% of total, up 9% YoY, reflecting the lumpiness of orphan launches. RareGuard, our AAV-based gene therapy for Pompe disease – comparable to BioMarin's Roctavian in hemophilia – generated $162 million, up 10% YoY. Volume grew modestly 6% YoY to 1,450 treatments, with U.S. patient starts at 420 – up 8% – driven by our expanded REMS program and center-of-excellence network, now 150 sites. EU volumes flat at 180 amid pricing negotiations in Italy, but Japan ramped 25% post-PMDA approval with J&J partnership. Adherence isn't volume-tracked here, but durability data shows 92% one-year transgene expression persistence.

Pricing drove 3% growth: U.S. net price at $2.1 million per treatment after 42% gross-to-net erosion from outcomes-based rebates tied to CK enzyme levels – similar to Novartis' Zolgensma model. Ex-U.S. net price up 5% on confidential discounts. Initiatives include our viral vector CMO scale-up with Lonza, targeting 50% capacity expansion by year-end, and a Phase 2 readout for a next-indication in Danon disease H2 2024, potentially doubling addressable patients to 2,500 globally.

In summary, volume drove 13% of our 18% total growth, price 5%, with gross-to-net at 44% overall – in line with industry peers like Regeneron amid IRA headwinds. Excluding a $25 million oncology inventory build, core growth was 15%. We're confident in our 20-22% FY24 product revenue guide, supported by 15+ label expansions, two BLA filings, and $1.2 billion cash for M&A.

Thank you, David, and good afternoon, everyone. As we wrap up a transformative Q3 for NovaBio Therapeutics, I'd like to dive deeper into our R&D investments, which remain the lifeblood of our long-term value creation in this high-stakes biotech landscape. For the quarter, R&D expenses came in at $385 million, up 18% year-over-year and representing 52% of our total revenue of $742 million. On a full-year basis through Q3, we've invested $1.12 billion in R&D— a robust 15% increase from the prior year—equating to 48% of revenues. This acceleration reflects not just inflation in clinical costs, which are up industry-wide by 10-12% due to supply chain pressures and talent competition, but our deliberate prioritization of high-conviction assets in oncology, immunology, and rare genetic diseases.

Let me break this down by key drivers and priorities. First, clinical-stage advancement accounted for 62% of our Q3 spend, or roughly $240 million, with the lion's share going to our three late-stage programs: Nova-347, our next-gen ADC in HER2-positive breast cancer; ImmunoGuard-12, a bispecific T-cell engager for rheumatoid arthritis; and GeneFix-Alpha for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. Nova-347's Phase III EMPOWER-3 trial, mirroring the success of Enhertu's real-world label expansions, hit 85% enrollment ahead of schedule, burning through $120 million this quarter on patient dosing and imaging endpoints. We're on track for topline data in H1 2025, with a PDUFA target in Q4 2025—positioning us for peak sales potential north of $2.5 billion, akin to Datopotamab deruxtecan's trajectory at Daiichi Sankyo/AstraZeneca.

Discovery and preclinical efforts took 28% of the spend, at $105 million, where we're leaning into modalities that de-risk our pipeline. We've allocated 40% of this bucket to cell and gene therapies, including our CRISPR-Cas9 in vivo editing platform for Duchenne muscular dystrophy—building on the momentum from Sarepta's Elevidys approval. Early data from our IND-enabling studies show 65% dystrophin expression in non-human primates, and we're partnering with Beam Therapeutics to co-develop next-gen base editors, sharing $50 million in milestone costs this year.

The remaining 10%, or $40 million, went to enabling technologies and manufacturing scale-up. Post the Ozempic/semaglutide supply crunch, we've front-loaded $25 million into our Singapore CDMO facility to derisk viral vector production for GeneFix-Alpha, ensuring CMC readiness for our BLA filing next year.

Regionally, our spend is strategically diversified: 55% in the US, anchored by our Cambridge, MA hub for oncology trials amid high patient accrual rates; 25% in Europe, leveraging the EMA's PRIME designation for ImmunoGuard-12 to accelerate orphan drug reviews; and 20% in Asia-Pacific, primarily China via our JV with Innovent Biologics. This partnership mirrors Pfizer's with BioNTech, yielding $30 million in cost-sharing for Nova-347's APAC arm while tapping into China's 30% YoY growth in oncology trial sites. Geopolitically, we're hedging US-China tensions by qualifying backup sites in Japan and South Korea.

Strategically, our priorities align with macro tailwinds: oncology remains 45% of our pipeline NPV, driven by the $200 billion+ TAM and ADC renaissance—think Gilead's Trodelvy hitting $1B in sales run-rate. Immunology gets 30%, capitalizing on the JAK inhibitor fatigue post-Xeljanz black-box warnings, with our bispecifics offering cleaner safety profiles. Rare diseases round out 25%, where pricing power like BioMarin's $3M+ per patient for VOXZOGO justifies the 20-25% success probability premium.

Looking ahead, we guide to full-year R&D of $1.45-1.50 billion, implying 5-8% sequential growth in Q4 as we lap easier comps and layer in milestone payments from our Regeneron collaboration on IL-33 targets. Risks? Clinical delays from inflation and IRA price caps could pressure margins, but our 18-month cash runway—bolstered by $800 million in non-dilutive financing—gives us flexibility. We're also exploring tuck-in M&A, like Horizon Therapeutics' $28B Vyzulta deal, to bolt on Phase II assets in neurology.

In short, this R&D intensity—among the highest in large-cap biotech, comparable to Moderna's 50%+ post-mRNA pivot—fuels our goal of 3-5 NMEs by 2028, delivering 20%+ CAGR in peak sales.

Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. I'll now turn to our operating expense analysis for the third quarter, where we continue to execute on our disciplined yet innovation-driven cost structure. As a reminder, NovaBio Therapeutics remains laser-focused on advancing our leadership in next-generation biologics, particularly in oncology and cardiometabolic therapies, amid a dynamic macro environment marked by persistent inflation in clinical trial costs, regulatory tailwinds from the FDA's accelerated pathways, and competitive pressures from peers like Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk in the GLP-1 space.

For Q3, total operating expenses came in at $452 million, representing a 14% year-over-year increase, or approximately 56% of our record $805 million in quarterly revenue – a slight deleveraging from 59% in the prior-year period. This reflects our strategic front-loading of investments into high-ROI R&D while maintaining SG&A efficiency through digital transformation and targeted sales force optimization. Sequentially, OpEx rose 8% from Q2, driven primarily by the ramp-up of our Phase 3 trials, but we remain on track for full-year OpEx of $1.85 billion to $1.95 billion, implying about 52-54% of guidance midpoint revenue.

Diving deeper into the components:

R&D Expenses: $305 million, up 22% YoY and 68% of total OpEx.  
This is the engine of our biotech franchise, and we're proud of the productivity here. The increase was led by a $45 million escalation in externalized clinical costs for our flagship assets: Nova-401, our bispecific T-cell engager in oncology – now in a global Phase 3 basket trial enrolling 1,200 patients across 15 countries, with topline data expected H1 2025 – and Nova-278, our once-weekly GLP-1/GIP dual agonist for obesity, mirroring the blockbuster trajectory of Mounjaro but with a superior cardiac safety profile based on interim CVOT data. We've allocated $120 million to these two programs alone this quarter, up 35% YoY, as we accelerate site activations in the U.S. and EU to mitigate any potential delays from the ongoing EMA review backlog.

We also advanced technical initiatives like our AI-powered drug discovery platform, in partnership with Insilico Medicine, which reduced hit-to-lead timelines by 40% for our three preclinical gene therapy candidates targeting rare cardiomyopathies. Manufacturing scale-up for our viral vector processes added $25 million in tech transfer costs, but this positions us ahead of peers like Sarepta in AAV production efficiency. Regionally, U.S. R&D spend was 55% of the total, buoyed by NIH grant funding; Europe at 25%, tempered by slower HTA reimbursements in Germany and France; and Asia-Pacific at 20%, where we're leveraging cost-effective CROs in China for early-phase work – a 50% YoY increase there to tap into the booming NMPA approvals for biosimilars.

Excluding one-time milestone payments to our CRISPR collaborator Editas Medicine ($15 million), core R&D grew 18% YoY, with productivity metrics improving: our R&D spend per pipeline asset down 12% to $28 million, thanks to portfolio prioritization – we divested two early-stage assets in Q2 for $50 million in non-dilutive capital.

SG&A Expenses: $138 million, up 8% YoY and 31% of total OpEx.  
Here, we're executing flawlessly on efficiency. The modest increase reflects a 15% expansion of our U.S. specialty sales force to 850 reps – focused on Nova-401's anticipated launch – but offset by a 22% reduction in travel and T&E via our Salesforce Einstein AI CRM implementation, which boosted rep productivity by 18% in key accounts. Marketing spend for Nova-278's pre-commercial activities rose $12 million, including patient access programs and KOL engagements ahead of our projected Q4 PDUFA.

Regionally, U.S. SG&A was 65% of the bucket, driven by DTC advertising compliant with the FDA's evolving digital ad guidelines; ex-U.S. at 35%, with Europe flat due to pricing pressures post-IEHP negotiations in the UK, and a strategic ramp in Japan where we're building out a 50-person team for Nova-401's J-code application. As a silver lining, our SG&A as a percentage of revenue improved to 17% from 20% YoY, outperforming the Amgen peer average of 19%, underscoring our leverage from the $2.1 billion in annualized product revenue run-rate.

Other Operating Expenses: $9 million, flat YoY.  
Primarily site maintenance and IP litigation settlements – minimal impact.

Key Trends and Strategic Insights:  
Looking forward, we're navigating industry headwinds like a 10-15% inflation in biologics raw materials (per IQVIA data) and talent competition for PhD-level scientists, with median comp up 12% industry-wide. Our countermeasures include a 25% shift to milestone-based CRO contracts, zero-based budgeting for non-core functions, and a $100 million share repurchase authorized last quarter to return capital amid our fortress balance sheet.

Strategically, in this era of patent cliffs – think Keytruda's 2028 expiry – we're doubling down on platform technologies: our ADC linker tech, licensed from Seagen pre-Pfizer acquisition, is yielding three INDs by 2025, with OpEx efficiency from reusable scaffolds. We're also monitoring biosimilar erosion on our legacy Humira-like TNF inhibitor, which shaved $8 million off SG&A via reduced promo budgets.

In summary, our OpEx profile balances aggressive innovation with fiscal prudence, positioning NovaBio for 25-30% EPS growth in FY25.

Now, I'll hand the call back to David.

David Thompson, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jane Doe, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and good morning. Sarah, great details on the product revenue breakdown—impressive volume lift on OncoVita despite biosimilar pressures. Can you expand on the pricing outlook, especially with more value-based agreements and IRA impacts? And how does that factor into your FY24 guide?

Sarah Jenkins, CFO:
Thanks, Jane. Appreciate the question. On pricing, as I noted, net ASP for OncoVita dipped slightly in the U.S. due to expanded 360-value-based deals now covering 45% of lives, which tie rebates to outcomes like progression-free survival. That's in line with peers amid IRA clawbacks, but our gross-to-net remains efficient at 44%. Ex-U.S., tender wins in China helped offset. This dynamic supports our confidence in the 20-22% FY24 product revenue guide, with volume from label expansions more than compensating. No changes there.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee, Morgan Stanley:
Good morning, team. David or Raj, on the R&D side, the Phase 3 progress for Nova-347 sounds promising. Could you provide more color on enrollment risks in APAC and the competitive landscape for ADCs post-Enhertu? Also, any updates on the CRISPR Duchenne program?

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
Thanks, Mike. On Nova-347's EMPOWER-3 trial, we're at 85% enrollment globally, with APAC contributing meaningfully through our Innovent JV—cost-sharing has de-risked that arm, and we're using backup sites in Japan/South Korea to hedge geopolitics. Competition in ADCs is fierce, but our payload differentiates with lower toxicities, targeting $2.5B+ peak similar to Trodelvy. For CRISPR Duchenne, IND-enabling data hit 65% dystrophin in NHPs; Beam partnership accelerates base editing. Topline preclinical H1 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Alex Kim, JPMorgan:
Hi, team. Sarah, your marketing ROI metrics are standout—4.8x blended. How sustainable is the digital shift amid sales force optimization, and any read-through to NeuroVex's 10% share in six months?

Sarah Jenkins, CFO:
Alex, great question. Sustainability comes from "PrecisionLaunch" AI segmenting HCPs into micro-cohorts for 24% routing gains, plus closed-loop Marketo automation. Digital now 45% of budget, countering industry sales force cuts. NeuroVex's ramp validates Launch360—DTC drove 19% NRx via Google surge, akin to Emgality. Expect continued 5x+ ROI as we scale.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There are no further questions at this time.

David Thompson, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Lisa Chen, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
